_comment: REAL LINES FROM THE GAME, not 'the quick brown fox'. Testing TTS on
neutral sentences tells you nothing — the whole question is whether a
model can deliver a threat quietly, land the emphasis on the right word,
and sound like the same person twice. Each line carries the emotional
direction the SIMULATION already knows, which is our unfair advantage:
we can tell the model how to say it because the game knows how the
Voices: American English, late 1980s / early 90s rust-belt port city.

lena.who: Lena, late 30s, the bar's bookkeeper. Dry, careful, has known the family twenty years. Never raises her voice.
lena.target: warm mid-range female, slight rasp, unhurried

rocco.who: Rocco, 50s, works the door. Night circle. Tired, decent, seen everything.

mara.who: Mara Ellis, 40s, police detective working a case on this street. Never threatens; does not need to.

crowd_m.who: An anonymous man on the street.

crowd_f.who: An anonymous woman on the street.

cases.direction: low, leaning in, certain of what he saw
cases.text: I'm telling you, he was down at the warehouse the night it went up.
There's a story going round that he keeps hours nobody keeps. Probably nothing.

cases.direction: quiet warning between friends, not a threat
cases.text: I'd keep that behind my teeth if I were you.

bored, end of a long shift, barely listening
cases.text: So which is it going to be?

cases.direction: grave, the most serious question she has ever asked him — SAME TEXT as same_line_bored, and the two takes must be obviously different
cases.text: So which is it going to be?

cases.direction: steady, laying it out on the counter between them, no drama
cases.text: Seven days. You've seen what it is now. Mickey never chose. He let the street choose for him, a week at a time, and it used him up.

cases.direction: polite, procedural, faintly bored — the menace is that there is none
cases.text: The inspection closes on day fourteen. Two days remain. You have been given what you asked for twice, and refused once.
You'll get used to it. We always do.

cases.direction: shutting a door on the conversation, not hostile
the numbers must sound spoken, not read — '$120' is 'a hundred and twenty', 'day 8' is 'day eight'
cases.text: Your name's in Mickey's book for $120, and day 8 is when he'd have asked.

_comment: THE DECISIVE TEST. Same voice, same character, ten lines. If a model
cannot produce ten takes that sound like ONE PERSON, it cannot voice a
character no matter how good any single line sounds. This is the test
texts: Mickey kept more than one set of books.
I've known better people do worse for less.
Don't ask me about the landlord.
I moved them because you asked me to.
Seven days, and you've seen what it is.
So which is it going to be?
